source: Derived independently from official HuggingFace config.json values; pinned by fitllm unit tests. An implementation conforms if every vector passes.

vectors.note: global 10L*2*4h*512d*2B*262144 + local 50L*2*16h*256d*2B*1024 = 20.78 GiB (public anchor)
heterogeneous head_dim: global 8L*2*1h*512d + sliding 40L*2*8h*256d (window 1024)
hybrid linear: only 16/64 full-attention layers carry KV
MLA: (kv_lora_rank 512 + rope 64) * 2B * 47L — single shared latent, NOT per-head K/V
past sliding window(128) only 12/24 full-attn layers grow: 2*8h*64d*2B*12L
hybrid: 10/40 full-attn layers only (30 linear carry no growing KV)
PLE residency: GPU weights = (5.1-2.349)B x 2B = 5.12 GB resident; 2.349B PLE (262144x256x35, config.json) lives in system RAM (llama.cpp #14430). Without PLE split this reads 'no' (12.96 GB).
standard GQA full attention: 2(K,V) x 8 kv-heads x 128 dim x 2 B x 80 layers x 262,144 = 85,899,345,920 B = 80.00 GiB exactly (tencent/Hy3 config.json)

hybrid Gated DeltaNet: KV only on the 16 full-attention layers of 64 = 2(K,V) x 4 kv-heads x 256 dim x 2 B x 16 L x 262,144 = 16.00 GiB exactly. Counting all 64 layers gives 68,719,476,736 B (4x too much) — the common naive-calculator error. Source: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B config.json layer_types + model card 'Hidden Layout: 16 x (3 x Gated DeltaNet -> 1 x Gated Attention)'

Gated DeltaNet fixed recurrent state (context-independent): per layer conv (16*128*2 + 48*128 = 10,240 conv_dim) x 4 kernel x 2 B = 81,920 + recurrent 48 v-heads x 128 x 128 x 4 B (mamba_ssm_dtype float32) = 3,145,728; x 48 linear layers = 154,927,104 B = 147.75 MiB. Shapes: transformers qwen3_next modeling (conv_dim = key_dim*2 + value_dim)
KV only on 23 full-attention layers of 92 = 2 x 4 x 256 x 2 B x 23 L x 262,144 = 23.00 GiB exactly (model card '23 x (3 x Gated DeltaNet -> 1 x Gated Attention)')
backfill guard — Qwen 3.6 27B shares the qwen3_5 DeltaNet dims with Qwen 3.8 27B (48 linear layers, 48 v-heads). KV total is unchanged by this component
standard full-attention GQA model must report exactly zero linear state — the new component may never leak into non-hybrid models

interleaved SWA: global 10 L x full ctx + local 30 L x window 512, all 2 x 8 kv-heads x 128 dim x 2 B = 4,096 B/layer/token -> 4,096 x 10 x 262,144 + 4,096 x 30 x 512 = 10,800,332,800 B. Source: poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1 config.json layer_types {full 10, sliding 30}, sliding_window 512
global 12 L + local 36 L (window 512) = 4,096 x 12 x 262,144 + 4,096 x 36 x 512 = 12,960,399,360 B. Model card: '48 layers in a 1:3 global-to-SWA ratio (12 global, 36 sliding, window 512)'
hybrid KV keeps 27.8B at Q4 comfortably on 32GB even at 32K context (~13.5 GiB free)
27.8B at Q4 does not fit a 16GB card even before context: weights alone ~12.9 GiB + 2.0 GiB KV. Chosen with ~2.5 GiB of margin so the vector is a stable answer-key entry, not a knife-edge

interleaved SWA 3:1 at native 1M ctx: all layers 2 x 4 kv-heads x 256 dim x 2 B = 4,096 B/layer/token -> global 9 L x 1,048,576 + local 27 L x window 512 = 4,096 x 9,437,184 + 4,096 x 13,824 = 38,654,705,664 + 56,623,104 = 38,711,328,768 B (36.05 GiB, vs 4.1B bf16 weights ~7.66 GiB — KV residency is the long-context bottleneck; a naive all-layers formula gives 4x = 144 GiB). Source: XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B config.json at revision 5e10fcc0286756aebf7c41dc52c1e42d95c70281 — layer_types {sliding_attention 27, full_attention 9}, sliding_window 512, num_key_value_heads 4, head_dim 256, max_position_embeddings 1048576

dense GQA, every one of the 64 layers keeps a full-context cache: 2 (K+V) x 8 kv-heads x head_dim 128 (hidden 4096 / 32 heads; config has no head_dim key) x 2 B = 4,096 B/layer/token -> 64 L x 4,096 = 262,144 B/token -> x 131,072 ctx = 34,359,738,368 B (exactly 32 GiB; bf16 weights are 58,553,540,608 B = 54.53 GiB, so at native context the F16 KV alone exceeds a 24 GiB card). A formula that uses the 32 query heads instead of the 8 kv-heads gives 4x = 137,438,953,472 B (128 GiB). Source: ibm-granite/granite-4.2-30b config.json at revision 9e668ce1c538387ef24d3644e9b0606647762636 (config blob identical at 8b445a5c315f32da0f89e1f648bfec0cd601b154): num_hidden_layers 64, num_attention_heads 32, num_key_value_heads 8, hidden_size 4096, max_position_embeddings 131072; no sliding_window, layer_types, kv_lora_rank or expert keys

dense GQA, all 42 layers keep a full-context cache: 2 (K+V) x 2 kv-heads x head_dim 128 x 2 B = 1,024 B/layer/token -> 42 L x 1,024 = 43,008 B/token -> x 131,072 ctx = 5,637,144,576 B (5.25 GiB). Using the 16 query heads instead of the 2 kv-heads gives 8x = 45,097,156,608 B (42 GiB). Source: openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B config.json at revision 12a3808a956f869c767195e9266b59c4d21d92e2 — model_type llama, num_hidden_layers 42, num_key_value_heads 2, head_dim 128, max_position_embeddings 131072.

hybrid Gated DeltaNet + Gated Attention: only the 10 full_attention layers keep a KV cache; the 30 linear_attention layers hold a fixed recurrent state that does not grow with ctx (modeled separately as linearState). 2 (K+V) x 2 kv-heads x head_dim 256 x 2 B = 2,048 B/layer/token -> 10 L x 2,048 = 20,480 B/token -> x 131,072 ctx = 2,684,354,560 B (2.50 GiB). Charging all 40 layers gives 4x = 10,737,418,240 B (10 GiB). Source: nex-agi/Nex-N2.5-mini config.json at revision 87420286149d9cce9bd46cd335ef9bda33c37c1b — layer_types {linear_attention 30, full_attention 10}, num_key_value_heads 2, head_dim 256.

same hybrid rule at a larger scale: 15 of 60 layers are full_attention. 2 (K+V) x 2 kv-heads x head_dim 256 x 2 B = 2,048 B/layer/token -> 15 L x 2,048 = 30,720 B/token -> x 131,072 ctx = 4,026,531,840 B (3.75 GiB). Charging all 60 layers gives 4x = 16,106,127,360 B (15 GiB). Note the KV is tiny next to the weights (396.8B logical params), which is the point: for this family the weight residency, not the cache, decides the verdict. Source: nex-agi/Nex-N2.5-Pro config.json at revision 0f389abfca976dcbab5c7638268d01cfe8ace4fe — layer_types {linear_attention 45, full_attention 15}, num_key_value_heads 2, head_dim 256.

GB10 unified memory, one unit: weights = max(114.6617856e9*4.25/8 + 2.1382144e9*4.8944/8 = 57.95, largest public Q4_K_M file 62,841,713,344 B = 58.53) = 58.53 GiB (the 114.6617856e9 shipped MXFP4 expert weights stay at their 4.25-bit storage (4-bit E2M1 + one E8M0 scale per 32) above 4.25 bits, and the weights are never counted below the largest public GGUF of that tier; no extra weight percentage on one GB10 since 2.21.4) + KV 0.29 + overhead 0.15*KV 0.04 + 8192*0.00003 0.25 + reserve 13.31 (128-121.69 OS-visible + 5.0 idle DGX OS + 2.0 runtime) = 72.41 of 128; headroom 20% = 25.6. Until 2.21.4 all 116.8e9 weights took the tier average (66.55 -> 80.43)

weights = max(114.6617856e9*4.25/8 + 2.1382144e9*6.5633/8 = 58.36, largest public Q6_K file 63,284,496,960 B = 58.94) = 58.94 GiB + KV 1.13 + overhead (0.15*KV 0.17 + 32768*0.00003 0.98) 1.15 + reserve 13.31 = 74.53 -> free 53.47 >= 25.6 headroom. Until 2.21.4 the whole 116.8e9 took the Q6_K average (89.24 -> 104.84, free 23.16 -> tight); a port that does so still says tight

117.562e9*6.5633/8 = 89.83 + KV(12 global x 2*8*128*2B*262144 + 36 sliding x 512) 12.07 + overhead (0.15*KV 1.81 + 262144*0.00003 7.86) 9.67 + reserve 13.31 = 124.88 of 128 -> free 3.12 < 25.6 headroom -> tight. Until 2.21.3 a further 12% of the weights (10.78) made it 135.66 -> no; public GB10 llama.cpp/Ollama allocation logs (fixtures/measured.json) show GGUF weights load at their file size, so one GB10 adds no weight percentage. A port that keeps it still says no

GB10 cluster, 2 units, tensor parallel 2: weights = largest public Q8_0 file 63,387,347,520 B = 59.03 GiB (above 114.6617856e9*4.25/8 + 2.1382144e9*8.5008/8 = 58.85; MXFP4 experts at their shipped 4.25 bits) + KV 0.29 (8 KV heads >= 2 units, no replication) + overhead 0.12*w 7.08 + 0.15*KV 0.04 + 8192*0.00003*2 units 0.49 + reserve 2*13.31 = 93.56 of 256 -> free 162.44 >= 51.2 headroom. One unit alone is also 'yes' now (72.92 of 128, vector v-gptoss120b-dgxspark128-q8-8k); with the Q8_0 average on all 116.8e9 weights it was 'no' (129.47 of 128)

4 units, 2 KV heads < 4 -> KV replicated x2: weights 392.68 + KV 3.75*2 = 7.50 + linear state 0.18 + overhead (0.12*w + 0.15*KV + 131072*0.00003*4) 63.98 + reserve 4*13.31 = 517.58 > 512. Without the replication and per-unit activation buffers a port would say 'tight' (501.47)

CSA2 shares KV across layers: only the 4 kv_source_layer_ids (2, 8, 14 at compress ratio 2; 20 at ratio 1) keep a compressed main KV (head_dim 512, one shared head) and indexer keys (index_head_dim 128); the other 36 layers keep only their sliding window and read the source's cache. Per token: 3 x (512 + 128) / 2 + 1 x (512 + 128) / 1 = 1,600 elements x 2 B (the reference code's bf16 buffers) = 3,200 B + 8 B Engram n-gram token history (NgramHashState.cache, int64 per position) = 3,208 B. The same 1,600 elements in DeepSeek's FP4 formats (main 1,280 x 0.5625 B + indexer 320 x 0.53125 B) give the 890 B/token the tech report states. Charging all 40 layers a 512-dim cache at 2 B gives 40,960 B/token (12.8x). Source: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 config.json at revision 1bae0e1088993b9b82de08f59de5be5a34e42170 and inference/model.py + inference/engram.py at the same revision.

3,208 B/token x 1,048,576 ctx = 3,363,831,808 B + sliding windows 128 tokens x 512 x 2 B x 43 layers (40 backbone + 3 DSpark draft blocks, all compress ratio 0 past layer 39) = 5,636,096 B + compressor fp32 state for the three ratio-2 sources 3 x 2 x (2 x 512) x 4 B = 24,576 B + the 512 MiB indexer prefill workspace (vLLM VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB default; vllm/envs.py at 2067297b2f15f0776be6d2a7e1b435bd20af60c1) = 536,870,912 B -> 3,906,363,392 B (3.64 GiB). Source: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 config.json at revision 1bae0e1088993b9b82de08f59de5be5a34e42170 and inference/model.py + inference/engram.py at the same revision.

V4 (CSA + HCA): every compressed layer owns its cache. compress_ratios over 43 layers = 2 x 0 (window only), 21 x 4 (CSA: 512-dim main KV + 128-dim indexer keys, both 1 per 4 tokens), 20 x 128 (HCA: 512-dim main KV, 1 per 128 tokens). Per token: 21 x (512 + 128) / 4 + 20 x 512 / 128 = 3,440 elements x 1 B = 3,440 B -> x 1,048,576 = 3,607,101,440 B + windows 128 x 512 x 1 B x 44 layers (incl. the MTP block) = 2,883,584 B + compressor fp32 state (CSA 21 x (2 x 8 x 1024 + 2 x 8 x 256) x 4 B + HCA 20 x 2 x 128 x 512 x 4 B) = 12,206,080 B + the 512 MiB indexer prefill workspace (vLLM VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB default; vllm/envs.py at 2067297b2f15f0776be6d2a7e1b435bd20af60c1) = 536,870,912 B -> 4,159,062,016 B (3.87 GiB). The state and the workspace do not shrink with --kv. Source: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash config.json and inference/model.py at revision 60d8d70770c6776ff598c94bb586a859a38244f1.

compress_ratios over 61 layers = 30 x 4 (CSA) and 31 x 128 (HCA; layers 0 and 1 are HCA here, unlike Flash). Per token: 30 x (512 + 128) / 4 + 31 x 512 / 128 = 4,924 elements x 2 B = 9,848 B. A uniform 61-layer x 512-dim cache would be 62,464 B/token (6.3x). Source: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro config.json at revision b5968e9190ef611bbf34a7229255be88a0e937c1.

standard GQA with a 1:3 full/sliding schedule: 16 full_attention layers keep the whole context and 46 sliding_attention layers keep 2,048 tokens. 2 (K+V) x 16 kv-heads x head_dim 64 x 2 B = 4,096 B/layer/token -> 16 x 4,096 x 1,048,576 = 68,719,476,736 B + 46 x 4,096 x 2,048 = 385,875,968 B -> 69,105,352,704 B (64.36 GiB). Using the 128 query heads gives 8x; charging all 62 layers the full context gives 3.9x. Source: unsloth/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B config.json at revision 49cade7b0c6ed297f0434229ac67eea5f9ae1220, the same git blob (e6df3a846ebfcb0d55c350c1e79e7886c65b7399) as the gated meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B original; attention per huggingface/transformers models/muse_spark at 487dcfa6ab1c294ce2695005108fdf19a63363eb.

weights = max(formula, released checkpoint 510,296,708,312 B = 475.25 GiB) = 475.25 GiB: the formula 557.17134336e9 shipped FP4 experts x 4.25 / 8 (never above their storage) + (763.2e9 - 557.17134336e9) x 4.8944 / 8 + Engram floor 196.6138496e9 x (8.25 - 4.8944) / 8 (Engram tables never below their FP8 + E8M0-scale storage) gives 469.87, and with no public Q4_K_M file known the weights are never counted below the release (the whole checkpoint resident: 552B backbone + Engram + DSpark and vision weights) + KV 2.119 (one KV head, replicated on all 4 units, incl. 0.5 GiB indexer workspace each) + overhead (0.12 x weights 57.03 + 0.15 x KV 0.32 + 8192 x 0.00003 x 4 units 0.98) 58.33 + reserve 4 x 13.31 = 588.94 > 512. A port that sizes the weights from the 552B backbone figure says yes

weights = max(283.467841536e9 shipped FP4 experts x 4.25 / 8 + (290.9e9 - 283.467841536e9) x 8.5008 / 8 = 147.61, released checkpoint 159,617,149,040 B = 148.66) = 148.66 GiB (no public Q8_0 file known) + KV 1.99 GiB per unit (incl. the 0.5 GiB indexer workspace) x 4 units = 7.95 + overhead 46.56 + reserve 53.24 = 256.40 -> free 255.60 >= 102.4 headroom. Until 2.21.4 all 290.9e9 weights took the Q8_0 average (287.88 -> 412.33, free 99.67 -> tight); a port that does so still says tight. The KV-replication boundary moved to two units: v-dsv4flash-2xdgxspark128-q8-144k

Mac 512GB, 4-bit: the 196.6B Engram tables stay at their FP8 + scale storage (8.25 bit): (763.2e9 - 196.6138496e9) x 0.5 + 196.6138496e9 x 1.03125 = 452.67 GiB weights + KV 0.53 + overhead 54.65 + macOS/runtime reserve 8.0 = 515.85 > 512. Quantizing the Engram tables to 4 bits as well (no runtime verified to do so) gives 406.89 -> yes.

one GB10, Q8_0: weights = max(114.6617856e9*4.25/8 + 2.1382144e9*8.5008/8 = 58.85, largest public Q8_0 file 63,387,347,520 B = 59.03) = 59.03 GiB (the 114.6617856e9 shipped MXFP4 expert weights stay at their 4.25-bit storage (4-bit E2M1 + one E8M0 scale per 32) above 4.25 bits, and the weights are never counted below the largest public GGUF of that tier; the ggml-org MXFP4 file is the same 59.03) + KV 0.29 + overhead 0.15*KV 0.04 + 8192*0.00003 0.25 + reserve 13.31 = 72.92 of 128 -> free 55.08 >= 25.6. A port that gives all 116.8e9 weights the Q8_0 average (115.59) says no (129.47 of 128)

117.562e9*6.5633/8 = 89.83 + KV(12 global x 2*8*128*2B*8192 + 36 sliding x 512) 0.45 + overhead (0.15*KV 0.07 + 8192*0.00003 0.25) 0.31 + reserve 13.31 = 103.89 of 128 -> free 24.11 < 25.6 headroom -> tight. A port that treats GB10 as a discrete card (12% weight share 10.78, 0.6 reserve, 5% headroom 6.4) says yes (101.96, free 26.04). Takes over this check from v-gptoss120b-dgxspark128-q6k-32k, whose MXFP4 weights no longer reach the headroom

weights = max(283.467841536e9 shipped FP4 experts x 4.25 / 8 + (290.9e9 - 283.467841536e9) x 8.5008 / 8 = 147.61, released checkpoint 159,617,149,040 B = 148.66) = 148.66 GiB + KV 1.4616 GiB per unit (incl. the 0.5 GiB indexer workspace) x 2 units (the single KV head, the compressed caches and the workspace are per tensor-parallel rank) = 2.92 + overhead (0.12 x weights 17.84 + 0.15 x KV 0.44 + 147456 x 0.00003 x 2 units 8.85) 27.12 + reserve 2 x 13.31 = 205.32 -> free 50.68 < 51.2 headroom -> tight. Counting the KV once gives free 52.36 -> yes; the Q8_0 average on all 290.9e9 weights gives no (361.26 of 256)
